subject: Seeming bug in edge case when an array dimension is zero

messages.author: 1718a05954397331
messages.subject: Seeming bug in edge case when an array dimension is zero
parts:
Dear Stanisticians,

There may be a corner case when passing data as an array with one of its dimensions being zero.

Witness the Stan code (parameters and model are dummies for this example) ::

data {
    int<lower=0> K;
    int<lower=1> L;
    int<lower=1> M;
    vector[K] x[L,M];
}

transformed data {
    print(x);
}

parameters {
    real y;
}

model {
    y ~ normal(0,1);
}

which gives me, executing under RStan (1.2.0) on Mac OS X 10.6 ::

> stan(file="stan_bug.stan", data=list(L=3, M=5, K=0, x=array(c(123,234,345), dim=c(3,5,0))))

TRANSLATING MODEL 'stan_bug' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'stan_bug' NOW.
Error in new_CppObject_xp(fields$.module, fields$.pointer, ...) : 
  variable does not exist; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=x; base type=vector_d
In addition: Warning message:
In max(abs(x)) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

Calling with K >= 1 works as expected and prints the right thing.

Obviously, this model does not arise by itself. It's part of a larger hierarchical panel regression model, and represents a special case where I have no covariates (just intercepts, which I need to model separately).

Any ideas on ensuring that there is a graceful "degradation" (i.e. not an error) in the base case where we end up with a vector[0]?

Warm regards,
+ Nicolas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Seeming bug in edge case when an array dimension is zero
parts:
Thanks for the report. It's a bug in either
the way we're passing data from RStan to Stan or
in the way the underlying Stan reader works with
null data. I'll isolate the problem and report
back.

- Bob

P.S. I still find R itself baffling.

For instance, the way I would've tried to
write a zero-sized array would've been this:

> array(c(),dim=c(3,5,0))
Error in array(c(), dim = c(3, 5, 0)) :
attempt to set an attribute on NULL

But alas,

> is.null(c())
[1] TRUE

This must be why Nicolas went with some dummy values
in the first argument to array(), even though it
ignores those values:

> x <- array(c(123,234,345), dim=c(3,5,0))
> dim(x)
[1] 3 5 0

The fact that the thing with dummy values works
seems to be tied up with R's broadcasting/slicing strategy.
It's happy to just drop unused elements of the data array.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Seeming bug in edge case when an array dimension is zero
parts:
In trying to replicate Nicolas's example, I ran into a
bug in Stan's code generator. The following model can be parsed
by stanc, but the generated code causes the compilation
error reported below.

--------------------------------------------------------
data {
vector[0] x;

--------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------
~/stan(master)$ mk ../temp4/zero
clang++ -I src -I lib/eigen_3.1.2 -I lib/boost_1.53.0 -Wall -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE
-DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS -Wno-unused-function -Wno-tautological-compare -c -O0 -o ../temp4/zero.o ../temp4/zero.cpp
../temp4/zero.cpp:39:37: error: ambiguous conversion for functional-style cast from 'int' to 'vector_d'
(aka 'Matrix<double, Eigen::Dynamic, 1>')
x = std::vector<vector_d>(1,vector_d(0));
^~~~~~~~~~
lib/eigen_3.1.2/Eigen/src/Core/Matrix.h:220:34: note: candidate constructor
EIGEN_STRONG_INLINE explicit Matrix(Index dim)
^
lib/eigen_3.1.2/Eigen/src/Core/Matrix.h:268:14: note: candidate constructor
explicit Matrix(const Scalar *data);
^
1 error generated.
make: *** [../temp4/zero.o] Error 1
~/stan(master)$
--------------------------------------------------------

This is easy to fix -- we just need to use

vector_d(Eigen::DenseIndex(0))

to resolve the overload and we're good to go.

But this wasn't the issue with Nicolas's model.
Zero-length arrays work as is, such as

real x[0];

I/O also works OK for the command-line version of Stan,
where I wrote this for a data file.

--------------------------------------------------------
x <- c()
--------------------------------------------------------

So it doesn't look like the issue is in the basic Stan I/O.

I don't know what the right workaround is in R, but I'm confident
we (and by that I mean Jiqiang) will sort it out for the next release.

- Bob

P.S. The Python interface for Stan is underway! More on that later.
